modules.name: core
modules.title: Platform Core Ontology
modules.description: Upper module for the application platform ontology: principals, resources, events, and XACML-style policy architecture roles. All domain modules import this module. Since 0.2.0: tenants (the platform itself being a distinguished tenant), capabilities, tenant-owned applications, and the closed delivery-channel vocabulary — platform-wide primitives promoted from the control-plane module while all terms are draft.
modules.blurb: Upper module: principals, tenancy, capabilities, applications, authorized parties, delivery channels and the XACML roles.

modules.name: authn
modules.title: Authentication Module
modules.description: Credentials, authentication events and methods, identity providers, and NIST SP 800-63 assurance levels (modelled as SKOS concepts with numeric ranks for comparison). Since 0.2.0: authentication journeys — governed definitions per delivery channel, and executions comprising the events a principal actually traversed; achieved assurance lives on the execution. Since 0.3.0: proof-of-possession keys, the confirmation binding of RFC 7800 as used by DPoP (RFC 9449), which sender-constrains sessions and tokens so a stolen artifact is useless without the private key.
modules.blurb: Credentials, identity providers, assurance levels, authentication journeys and issuer-scoped subject identifiers.

modules.name: session
modules.title: Session Module
modules.description: Sessions, tokens, lifecycle states, and the binding between a session and its originating authentication. Since 0.2.0 sessions are established by an authentication journey EXECUTION rather than a single event (a structural retarget performed while all terms are draft); step-up elevations are further executions on the same session, and the effective AAL is the latest successful execution's. Since 0.3.0: session handles — the opaque value a cookie carries — and DPoP-style sender constraining, so a handle identifies a session while the proof-of-possession key authenticates the presenter.
modules.blurb: Sessions established by journey executions, step-up elevations, and tokens carrying both ends of their journey.

modules.name: ingress
modules.title: Ingress Module
modules.description: Gateways, listeners, routes, TLS termination, and upstream services. Deliberately implementation-independent: the terms describe the network entry model itself, not any particular gateway product or API. Since 0.2.0: route matching by domain and path, and the binding from a route to the tenant it serves — the configuration from which ingress resolves tenant context, and therefore the root of tenant.access.
modules.blurb: Network entry: gateways, listeners, routes, TLS termination and upstream services — deliberately implementation-independent.

modules.name: authz
modules.title: Authorization Module
modules.description: ABAC-first authorization: policies, rules, attribute assertions with provenance, roles, decisions, and obligations. Vocabulary aligns to XACML architecture. Since 0.2.0: the closed, platform-owned entitlement dimension scheme and entitlement grants (machine-generated projections of upstream governance, distributed to ingress), plus ingress admission decisions. A grant is a conferral with lifecycle and derivation — distinct from an attribute assertion, which is an observation.
modules.blurb: ABAC-first authorization plus the platform-owned coarse-grained layer: dimensions, grants, actions and admission decisions.

modules.name: control-plane
modules.title: Control Plane Module
modules.description: Control plane components, administrative scopes, and meta-authorization: policy/config change events and their human approvals. Encodes the 'agents execute, humans authorize' invariant, with management vs. capability control planes separating governance from actuation. Since 0.3.0: the scope tree with locality and scope-dependent approval rigor; capability subscriptions, bundles, hard dependencies, and per-scope offerings (no cross-scope parity); application enablement, observed-then-confirmed capability requirements, and portals. Tenant and Capability were promoted to core in this version, while draft.
modules.blurb: Two-tier planes, the scope tree, and the chain from subscriptions and offerings to declarations and mutations.

terms.name: Application
terms.definition: An independently developed application owned by exactly one tenant (possibly the platform tenant), reachable through ingress once enabled, and consuming platform capabilities per its confirmed requirements. What a subject may do inside the application is application-owned (Level 3) and deliberately out of this ontology's scope.

constraints.message: An application must be owned by exactly one tenant (the platform tenant for platform-owned applications).

terms.name: AuthorizedParty
terms.label: Authorized party
terms.definition: The governed registration of one unit of request-originating software — a portal's web or mobile front, or a headless API/agent consumer — owned by exactly one tenant, bound to exactly one delivery channel, holding revocable credentials, and the party to which tokens are issued (the azp claim). The evidence ingress resolves a request's channel from; never the running software instance, and never the party the token is addressed to (that is the audience).
terms.editorialNote: Named for the azp claim it anchors. Reinstated as the uniform azp target after Portal-only left token→client binding without a single-ranged home. Recorded reservations: 'Party' is banking master-data vocabulary for customers — this class is software registrations, not persons; and a registration is 'authorized' only in azp's token-time sense. The word 'client' remains reserved for the firm's business meaning; CallerRegistration and SoftwareRegistration were the runner-up names.

constraints.message: An authorized party must be registered by exactly one tenant.
An authorized party must be bound to exactly one delivery channel — the binding ingress derives channel evidence from.
An authorized party acts as at most one workload principal (headless parties exactly one by convention; portal fronts none).

terms.name: Capability
terms.definition: A platform offering provided to tenants via subscription (managed database, messaging, unified ingress). Each capability is governed by exactly one capability control plane; where it is available is stated per scope by capability offerings, with no cross-scope parity assumed.

constraints.message: Capability participates in a circular capability dependency — hard dependencies must form a DAG.

terms.name: DeliveryChannel
terms.definition: The delivery avenue through which platform capabilities are consumed, determinable by ingress from the registration presenting the request — never from a self-asserted claim. Members are individuals in a closed, platform-owned scheme.

vocabulary.label: AI agent
vocabulary.note: Delegation semantics deliberately deferred; see the agent-channel backlog questions.

terms.name: HumanPrincipal
terms.definition: A principal representing a human user, identified via the firm's directory (e.g., SID/HR identifier).

terms.name: PlatformEvent
terms.definition: An auditable occurrence on the platform. Subclassed by domain modules (AuthenticationEvent, PolicyDecision, PolicyChangeEvent).

constraints.message: Every platform event must have exactly one occurrence timestamp.
performedBy must reference a Principal.

terms.name: PlatformTenant
terms.definition: The distinguished singleton tenant representing the platform itself. Platform-owned applications are owned by it, and it holds capability subscriptions like any tenant, keeping every ownership and coverage rule uniform. Exactly one individual is expected (stewardship-enforced).

terms.name: PolicyAdministrationPoint
terms.definition: Component through which policy is authored and managed (XACML PAP).

terms.name: PolicyDecisionPoint
terms.definition: Component that evaluates policy and renders authorization decisions (XACML PDP).

terms.name: PolicyEnforcementPoint
terms.definition: Component that intercepts access and enforces PDP decisions (XACML PEP).

terms.name: PolicyInformationPoint
terms.definition: Component that supplies attribute values used in policy evaluation (XACML PIP).

terms.name: Principal
terms.definition: An entity that can be authenticated and to which authorization decisions apply.

constraints.message: Every principal must carry exactly one canonical firm-wide identifier.

terms.name: Resource
terms.definition: Anything access to which is governed by policy: services, routes, data assets, control-plane operations.

constraints.message: Resource has no governing policy — flag for stewardship review.

terms.name: Tenant
terms.definition: An organizational unit onboarded to the platform, to which subscriptions, applications, entitlement grants, and data planes are scoped.

terms.name: WorkloadPrincipal
terms.definition: A principal representing a non-human workload (service, agent, job), identified via a workload identity such as a SPIFFE ID.

terms.name: displayName
terms.definition: Human-readable label for governance and stewardship UIs.

terms.name: identifier
terms.definition: Canonical firm-wide identifier for the subject (SPIFFE ID for workloads; directory identifier for humans).

terms.name: occurredAtTime
terms.definition: Timestamp at which a platform event occurred.

terms.name: validFrom
terms.definition: Start of a validity window (attribute assertions, subscriptions, subject identifiers). Promoted from authz while draft — generic temporal vocabulary belongs in the upper module.

terms.name: validUntil
terms.definition: End of a validity window.

terms.name: boundToChannel
terms.definition: The single delivery channel an authorized party is bound to. Ingress derives a request's channel from this binding — never from a self-asserted claim.

terms.name: enforcedBy
terms.definition: Links a resource or route to the policy enforcement point that mediates access to it.

terms.name: governedBy
terms.definition: Links a resource to a policy that governs access to it.

terms.name: hasActingIdentity
terms.definition: Principal under whose identity a resource acts: a control plane component's SPIFFE workload identity, or the workload principal behind a headless authorized party (client-credentials flows). Resources cannot be principals; their acts are performed by this principal. Portal fronts carry none — their requests act as the authenticated human's principal. Promoted from control-plane while draft.

terms.name: ownedBy
terms.definition: Tenant that owns an application, portal, or authorized party — exactly one (enforced in SHACL); ownership transfer is a supersession of declarations, never co-ownership. Platform assets are owned by the distinguished platform tenant.

terms.name: performedBy
terms.definition: Links a platform event to the principal that performed it. Typing enforced in SHACL, not via rdfs:domain/range.

terms.name: targetsResource
terms.definition: Links an event or policy to the resource it concerns.

terms.name: AssuranceLevel
terms.definition: NIST SP 800-63 assurance level (IAL/AAL/FAL), modelled as an individual with an integer rank for ordering in SHACL-SPARQL constraints.

terms.name: AuthenticationEvent
terms.definition: A discrete attempt (successful or failed) to authenticate a principal.

constraints.message: An authentication event must concern exactly one principal.
An authentication event must record at least one authentication method from the controlled vocabulary.
An authentication event must record whether it succeeded.
A successful authentication event must record an achieved assurance level.

terms.name: AuthenticationJourneyDefinition
terms.definition: A governed template of an authentication flow (e.g., 'web-default: password then OTP, yields AAL2'), bound to the delivery channels it serves. Changes to definitions are security-relevant desired state and flow through the control plane's declaration and approval machinery.

terms.name: AuthenticationJourneyExecution
terms.definition: A principal's concrete traversal of a journey definition, comprising the authentication events actually performed. Sessions are established by executions, and step-up elevations are further executions on the same session; achieved assurance is a property of completing the flow, not of any single step.

constraints.message: A journey execution must comprise at least one authentication event.
A journey execution must concern exactly one principal.
A journey execution must record whether it succeeded.
Journey execution follows no governed definition — flag for stewardship review.
A successful journey execution must record an achieved assurance level.

terms.name: AuthenticationMethod
terms.definition: A controlled-vocabulary concept for how authentication was performed. Members are individuals, not subclasses.

terms.name: Credential
terms.definition: An artifact used to prove an identity claim (password record, FIDO2 key registration, client certificate, workload SVID).

constraints.message: A credential must be bound to a principal or an authorized party.
A credential must have an issuing identity provider.

terms.name: IdentityProvider
terms.definition: A system that asserts principal identities (enterprise IdP, workload identity issuer).

terms.name: ProofOfPossessionKey
terms.label: Proof-of-possession key
terms.definition: The public half of a key pair whose private half the presenting software holds and proves possession of per request (DPoP, RFC 9449; confirmation claim, RFC 7800). Binding a session or token to such a key sender-constrains it: the artifact alone is no longer sufficient, so a stolen handle or token cannot be replayed by a party that does not hold the key. Distinct from a credential — it is generated by the presenter rather than issued by an identity provider, and it proves continuity of possession rather than an identity claim.

constraints.message: A proof-of-possession key must carry exactly one JWK thumbprint — it is what a presented proof is compared against.

terms.name: SubjectIdentifier
terms.definition: A first-class naming fact: at one issuer, one subject value denotes one principal (RFC 9493 / OIDC sub). Read in reverse at resolution time — a token or security event carries the subject; this node yields the principal. Optionally pairwise: scoped to the authorized party the issuer minted it for. Not a credential (it proves nothing and is presented by no one) and not an attribute assertion (it resolves an unknown subject rather than describing a known principal).

constraints.message: A subject identifier must carry exactly one subject value.
A subject identifier must be scoped to exactly one issuer.
A subject identifier must denote exactly one principal.
A subject identifier must name its RFC 9493 format.
A pairwise subject identifier is scoped to at most one authorized party.
Same issuer, subject value, and party scope denote more than one principal — subject-identifier collision.

terms.name: SubjectIdentifierFormat
terms.definition: RFC 9493 subject identifier format; members are individuals in a closed scheme, extended by MINOR bump.

vocabulary.label: email
vocabulary.note: Email subjects are recyclable by issuers — validity windows matter most here.

terms.name: assuranceRank
terms.definition: Integer rank of an assurance level, used for ordered comparison in constraints (AAL1=1, AAL2=2, AAL3=3).

terms.name: keyAlgorithm
terms.definition: Signature algorithm the proof-of-possession key is used with (for example ES256).

terms.name: keyThumbprint
terms.definition: JWK SHA-256 thumbprint identifying a proof-of-possession key (RFC 7638) — the jkt value a confirmation claim carries. Identifies the key without disclosing it, and is what an enforcement point compares a presented proof against.

terms.name: subjectValue
terms.definition: The subject string as the issuer mints it (the sub claim value, an email, an opaque handle).

terms.name: succeeded
terms.definition: Whether the authentication event or journey execution succeeded.

terms.name: achievedAssuranceLevel
terms.definition: AAL achieved by a successful authentication event or journey execution. For executions, this is the flow's outcome — password alone achieves nothing; password+OTP achieves AAL2.

terms.name: atIssuer
terms.definition: Identity provider within whose namespace a subject identifier is unique.

terms.name: authenticatedPrincipal
terms.definition: The principal that the authentication event concerns.

terms.name: comprisesEvent
terms.definition: Authentication event that is a step of a journey execution. Single-step flows (passkey, client credentials) are one-event executions.

terms.name: confirmedByKey
terms.definition: Proof-of-possession key a session or token is sender-constrained to — the cnf binding of RFC 7800, carried as cnf.jkt under DPoP. A session or token without one is a bearer artifact: whoever holds it can use it.

terms.name: credentialOf
terms.definition: Principal to which a credential is bound.

terms.name: followsDefinition
terms.definition: Journey definition a journey execution traversed.

terms.name: identifierFormat
terms.definition: RFC 9493 format of a subject identifier.

terms.name: identifies
terms.definition: Principal a subject identifier denotes. One (issuer, value, party-scope) combination must never identify two principals (collision invariant, SHACL); one principal may hold several identifiers, even at one issuer (linking, migration).

terms.name: issuedBy
terms.definition: Identity provider that issued a credential or asserted an identity.

terms.name: scopedToParty
terms.definition: Authorized party a pairwise subject identifier is minted for; absent means the identifier is public across the issuer's parties.

terms.name: servesChannel
terms.definition: Delivery channel a journey definition serves.

terms.name: usedCredential
terms.definition: Credential presented in an authentication event.

terms.name: usedMethod
terms.definition: Authentication method concept used in an authentication event.

terms.name: AccessToken
terms.definition: Token presented to resource servers to authorize requests (e.g., OAuth 2.0 access token).

terms.name: IDToken
terms.definition: OIDC ID token asserting the authentication of a principal.

terms.name: RefreshToken
terms.definition: Token exchanged for new access tokens without re-authentication.

terms.name: Session
terms.definition: A bounded period of authenticated interaction between a principal and the platform, established by an authentication event.

constraints.message: Every session must be established by exactly one authentication journey execution (single-step flows are one-event executions).
Session elevations must be authentication journey executions.
Every session must be bound to exactly one principal.
Every session must have exactly one lifecycle state.
Every session must have an expiry.
Session principal must match the principal of its originating authentication event.
An active session must originate from a successful authentication journey execution.
Session is not sender-constrained: no proof-of-possession key confirms it, so a stolen handle alone would be replayable.
Session issued a token bound to a different key, or to no key at all — sender constraining must not be lost at token issuance.
One proof-of-possession key confirms sessions bound to different principals — key confusion.

terms.name: SessionHandle
terms.definition: The opaque value presented to identify a session — typically carried in a cookie. It identifies but does not authenticate: under DPoP-style sender constraining the presenter must also prove possession of the session's confirmation key, so a stolen handle alone grants nothing. A handle must resolve to exactly one session (enforced in SHACL); several may resolve to one session across rotations.

constraints.message: A session handle must resolve to exactly one session — an ambiguous handle is a session-fixation hazard.

terms.name: SessionState
terms.definition: Lifecycle state of a session; members are individuals (Active, Expired, Revoked, Suspended) rather than subclasses.

terms.name: Token
terms.definition: A signed artifact carrying claims, issued within a session.

constraints.message: Every token must have an expiry.
Every token must be issued to exactly one authorized party (the azp claim) — without it, channel evidence and azp-mismatch audits are unanswerable.

terms.name: expiresAt
terms.definition: Instant at which the session or token expires.

terms.name: notBefore
terms.definition: Instant before which the session or token is not valid.

terms.name: boundToPrincipal
terms.definition: Principal to which the session is bound.

terms.name: elevatedBy
terms.definition: A step-up elevation journey execution performed within this session after establishment. The session's effective AAL is the latest successful execution's (establishing or elevating); elevation freshness is a policy concern, not session structure.

terms.name: establishedBy
terms.definition: The authentication journey execution that established this session. Mandatory, exactly one (enforced in SHACL). Retargeted from AuthenticationEvent to AuthenticationJourneyExecution in 0.2.0, while draft.

terms.name: hasState
terms.definition: Current lifecycle state of the session.

terms.name: issuedTo
terms.definition: Authorized party the token was issued to — the azp claim: who may PRESENT the token. Mandatory, exactly one (SHACL); the hop that makes channel evidence and azp-mismatch audits answerable.

terms.name: issuedToken
terms.definition: Token issued within this session.

terms.name: resolvesToSession
terms.definition: Session a presented handle identifies. Exactly one (enforced in SHACL) — a handle resolving to two sessions is a session-fixation hazard.

terms.name: tokenAudience
terms.definition: Resource (audience) for which a token is intended — the aud claim: who may ACCEPT the token. The opposite end of the token's journey from issuedTo.

terms.name: Gateway
terms.definition: A network entry point into the platform, exposing one or more listeners through which external traffic arrives.

constraints.message: A gateway must expose at least one listener.

terms.name: Listener
terms.definition: A protocol/port binding on a gateway.

constraints.message: A listener must have exactly one valid port.
Listener protocol must be one of HTTPS, TLS, TCP, HTTP.
Listener uses plaintext HTTP — confirm this is an internal redirect-only listener.

terms.name: Route
terms.definition: A rule mapping matched traffic on a gateway to an upstream service.

constraints.message: Route binds a tenant but declares no hostname — tenant context cannot be resolved from an address that is not stated.
Two routes bind the same domain and path to different tenants — one address must resolve to exactly one tenant.
Route binds a tenant with no route-binding declaration behind it — tenant resolution must be governed, not configured out of band.
A route must forward to at least one upstream service.
Every route must be mediated by exactly one policy enforcement point before its upstream.

terms.name: TLSConfiguration
terms.definition: TLS settings applied at a listener, including where TLS terminates relative to policy enforcement.

terms.name: UpstreamService
terms.definition: A backend service to which routes forward traffic.

terms.name: hostname
terms.definition: Domain a route matches. Together with the path prefix it forms the address a tenant is reached at; a tenant-bound route must carry one (enforced in SHACL).

terms.name: pathPrefix
terms.definition: Path prefix a route matches within its domain. Absent means the whole domain; present, it lets one domain serve several tenants or applications at different paths.

terms.name: port
terms.definition: Port number of a listener.

terms.name: protocol
terms.definition: Protocol of a listener (HTTPS, TLS, TCP).

terms.name: terminatesTLS
terms.definition: Whether TLS terminates at this listener (true) or is passed through (false).

terms.name: boundToTenant
terms.definition: Tenant that traffic matching this route is resolved to. This binding — not any token claim — is how ingress establishes tenant context, which makes it the root of tenant.access: whoever can change it changes who a request is treated as. Changes must be governed by a route-binding declaration (enforced in SHACL), and no domain and path may bind to two tenants.

terms.name: exposesRoute
terms.definition: Route attached to a gateway or listener.

terms.name: hasListener
terms.definition: Listener exposed by a gateway.

terms.name: hasTLSConfiguration
terms.definition: TLS configuration applied to a listener.

terms.name: routesTo
terms.definition: Upstream service to which a route forwards traffic.

terms.name: Action
terms.definition: An operation a policy decision evaluates — the action slot of the AuthZEN/XACML tuple (subject, action, resource → decision). Members are individuals in a closed, platform-owned scheme; application verbs (transfer, approve) belong to Level-3 application authorization and must never appear here (guard invariant).

vocabulary.label: Access
vocabulary.definition: Cross a platform or application boundary — the admission action.

vocabulary.label: Administer
vocabulary.definition: Mutate platform configuration or policy — control-plane operations.

terms.name: AttributeAssertion
terms.definition: A first-class attribute statement about a principal or resource: name, value, issuer, and validity window. Attributes carry provenance rather than being baked into role hierarchies.

constraints.message: An attribute assertion must have exactly one name.
An attribute assertion must have a value.
An attribute assertion must have an authoritative issuer — attributes without provenance cannot be used in decisions.
An attribute assertion must describe exactly one principal.

terms.name: DecisionOutcome
terms.definition: XACML decision outcome; members are individuals.

terms.name: EntitlementDimension
terms.definition: A coarse-grained access dimension ingress validates at the platform boundary. Members are individuals in a closed, platform-owned scheme; applications cannot introduce dimensions — extension is a deliberate MINOR-versioned act behind security-architecture review.

terms.name: EntitlementGrant
terms.definition: A conferral of platform access to a tenant on one entitlement dimension, with a value and validity window. Always the materialized projection of upstream governance (a subscription, tenant registration, or application enablement) distributed to ingress — never hand-authored (enforced in SHACL). The token is evidence; the grant is authority.

constraints.message: An entitlement grant must confer access to exactly one tenant.
An entitlement grant must name exactly one dimension from the platform-owned scheme.
An entitlement grant must carry a derivation link to its governing source — hand-authored grants are forbidden; grants are projections.
Grant has no distribution timestamp — staleness queries cannot cover it.

terms.name: IngressAdmissionDecision
terms.definition: A Level-1/Level-2 decision at the ingress policy enforcement point: subject → action → target → decision (AuthZEN-aligned), evaluated against distributed entitlement grants, with the channel derived from the presenting registration. The evaluated policy is the platform admission policy — the versioned unit of authorization logic the distributed grant configuration realizes — so the policy reference every decision must carry is honest, not synthetic.

constraints.message: An admission decision must arrive via exactly one channel, derived from the presenting registration.
An admission decision must evaluate at least one entitlement grant — admission without grants is admission without authority.
Admission decision evaluated a tenant's grants for a principal holding no active membership in that tenant.

terms.name: Obligation
terms.definition: An action the enforcement point must perform alongside enforcing a decision (log, step-up, watermark).

terms.name: Policy
terms.definition: A named, versioned unit of authorization logic governing one or more resources.

constraints.message: A policy must contain at least one rule.

terms.name: PolicyDecision
terms.definition: An evaluation of policy for a specific access request, with an outcome.

constraints.message: A policy decision must have exactly one outcome.
A policy decision must reference the policy it evaluated.
A policy decision must evaluate exactly one action — the AuthZEN tuple is incomplete without it.
Decision evaluates an action outside the platform-owned action vocabulary — application verbs are Level-3 and must not reach platform decisions.
Permit decision violates policy assurance requirement: the session's authentication AAL is below the policy's required AAL.

terms.name: PolicyRule
terms.definition: A single rule within a policy, with an effect (permit/deny) and conditions over attributes.

constraints.message: A rule must have exactly one effect: 'permit' or 'deny'.

terms.name: Role
terms.definition: A named collection of permissions; retained for RBAC interop, but modelled as one source of attribute assertions among others.

terms.name: attributeName
terms.definition: Name of the asserted attribute (e.g., 'lineOfBusiness', 'clearance').

terms.name: attributeValue
terms.definition: Value of the asserted attribute.

terms.name: distributedAt
terms.definition: Instant this grant projection was last distributed to the enforcement point; anchors staleness queries.

terms.name: effect
terms.definition: Effect of a rule: 'permit' or 'deny'.

terms.name: entitlementValue
terms.definition: Value a grant confers on its dimension (e.g., 'US' on region, 'prod' on environment, 'web' on channel).

terms.name: aboutPrincipal
terms.definition: Principal an attribute assertion describes.

terms.name: assertedBy
terms.definition: Authoritative source (PIP, IdP, HR system) that issued an attribute assertion.

terms.name: decisionOutcome
terms.definition: Outcome concept of a policy decision.

terms.name: derivedFrom
terms.definition: Upstream governance object a grant was projected from: a subscription, an application enablement, an authorized-party registration (channel grants), or — once modelled — the tenant onboarding record (platform/tenant grants). Mandatory: a grant with no derivation is a hand-authored grant, which violates.

terms.name: evaluatedAction
terms.definition: The action a policy decision evaluated — exactly one per decision (SHACL), drawn from the platform-owned action scheme. AuthZEN's action name is the concept's skos:notation.

terms.name: evaluatedGrant
terms.definition: Entitlement grant an admission decision evaluated.

terms.name: evaluatedPolicy
terms.definition: Policy evaluated to produce a decision.

terms.name: grantedTo
terms.definition: Tenant to which an entitlement grant confers access.

terms.name: hasRule
terms.definition: Rule contained in a policy.

terms.name: imposesObligation
terms.definition: Obligation attached to a rule or decision.

terms.name: onDimension
terms.definition: Entitlement dimension a grant confers access on; must be drawn from the platform-owned scheme.

terms.name: requestingPrincipal
terms.definition: Principal whose access request the decision concerns.

terms.name: requiredAssuranceLevel
terms.definition: Minimum AAL a policy requires of the session's originating authentication.

terms.name: viaChannel
terms.definition: Delivery channel through which an admission decision's request arrived, derived from the presenting registration.

terms.name: withinSession
terms.definition: Session in which the access request was made.

terms.name: AdministrativeScope
terms.definition: A bounded set of resources over which administrative authority is granted (tenant, namespace, line of business).

terms.name: ApplicationEnablement
terms.definition: A desired-state declaration enabling an application within the declaration's scope. Enablement inherits the full declaration machinery — scope, approval rigor, supersession; an application is enabled where a current, approved enablement says so, gated on its owner's subscription and offering coverage.

constraints.message: Application enablement exceeds its owner's active subscriptions: a confirmed capability requirement has no active subscription covering it.
Application enablement's scope is not covered by any offering of a confirmed required capability — enabled where the capability does not exist.

terms.name: CapabilityBundle
terms.definition: A named set of capabilities offered for subscription together. Bundles are sales-time convenience: subscribing to one expands to per-capability subscriptions, materialized; enforcement and reachability never see bundles.

terms.name: CapabilityControlPlane
terms.definition: A control plane governing one platform capability, and the designated writer that actuates governed desired state into that capability's data planes.

constraints.message: A capability control plane must govern exactly one capability.
A capability control plane must have a workload acting identity so its writes are attributable.
Capability control plane administers the scope containing its own desired-state declarations — self-governance loop.

terms.name: CapabilityOffering
terms.definition: Governed intent that a capability is offered in a scope. No cross-scope parity is assumed: a capability exists where an offering says it does. Data planes are actuation and must conform: deployed-where-not-offered violates; offered-but-undeployed is launch tracking.

constraints.message: Capability offering sits in a scope where a hard dependency lacks a covering offering — an unfulfillable promise.

terms.name: CapabilityRequirement
terms.definition: A capability an application requires, proposed by observed usage and confirmed by a human approval — 'agents observe, humans confirm'. Only confirmed requirements gate enablement; drift against live observation is watched in both directions.

terms.name: CapabilityUseObservation
terms.definition: A windowed aggregate observation, ingested from telemetry, that an application exercised a capability during a time window. Kept in-graph so requirement-drift questions stay answerable in CI; never per-request.

terms.name: ChangeApproval
terms.definition: An approval attached to a change event, given by a principal. Every policy change must carry at least one approval by a human principal (enforced in SHACL).

constraints.message: An approval must be given by exactly one principal.
An approval must be timestamped.

terms.name: ControlPlaneComponent
terms.definition: A component that manages platform configuration or policy (API server, policy service, gateway controller, MCP router control loop).

terms.name: DataPlane
terms.definition: A runtime plane realizing one capability and serving zero or more tenants; mutated only by its capability control plane's acting identity (sole-writer, enforced in SHACL).

constraints.message: A data plane must realize exactly one capability.
Data plane realizes a capability in a scope no offering covers — deployed where not offered.

terms.name: DataPlaneMutation
terms.definition: A write into a data plane performed by a control plane's acting identity, realizing a desired-state declaration.

constraints.message: A data-plane mutation must reference exactly one mutated data plane.
A data-plane mutation must realize a governed desired-state declaration — orphan write.
Data-plane mutation executed by a principal that is not the acting identity of the data plane's designated writer — sole-writer invariant.
Data-plane mutation targets a data plane outside the declaration's scope — scoped governance is not optional.
Mutation realizes a superseded declaration — reconciler catching up to stale intent; route to stewardship.

terms.name: DesiredStateDeclaration
terms.definition: A governed statement of intended data-plane state, declared through the management control plane. Data-plane mutations must trace to one (no orphan writes).

constraints.message: A desired-state declaration must be declared through exactly one management control plane.
A declaration must be bound to exactly one administrative scope — global intent names the root scope explicitly.
Declaration lacks human approval, but its scope requires human approval — rigor is inherited down the scope tree.
Declaration provisions capability state for a tenant without a justifying subscription — commercial intent must precede technical intent.

terms.name: JourneyDefinitionChange
terms.definition: A desired-state declaration changing an authentication journey definition. Journey definitions are security-relevant desired state; this subclass gives their changes scope, approval rigor, and supersession through the standard declaration machinery.

terms.name: ManagementControlPlane
terms.definition: The control plane that owns the governance layer: tenant registration, entitlement configuration, and desired-state declarations. It defines; it never actuates a data plane (enforced in SHACL).

constraints.message: The management control plane must not actuate a data plane directly — governance is separated from actuation (tier skipping).

terms.name: MembershipState
terms.definition: Lifecycle state of a tenant membership; members are individuals (Requested, Active, Suspended, Terminated). Kept separate from subscription and session state vocabularies: overlapping member names do not make them one vocabulary, and each must be able to evolve independently.

terms.name: PolicyChangeEvent
terms.definition: A mutation of authorization policy or security-relevant configuration.

constraints.message: A policy change event must reference the policy it changed.
Policy change has no change-management ticket reference — flag for audit follow-up.
Policy change lacks approval by a human principal — agents execute, humans authorize.

terms.name: Portal
terms.definition: A tenant-owned presentation grouping of applications, fronted by one or more authorized parties — one per delivery channel it is presented on (the web front and the iOS front of one portal are two authorized parties, each with its own credentials and revocation). Presentation only: admission stays per-application and the enforcement vocabulary never sees portals.

constraints.message: A portal must be fronted by at least one authorized party — one per delivery channel it is presented on.
A portal must be owned by exactly one tenant.
Portal is fronted by a party owned by a different tenant — fronts and portal share one owner.
Portal groups an application owned by another tenant — a portal may present its owner's applications and platform-owned applications only.
Portals of the same tenant have diverging application sets — divergence may be intentional (mobile subset); route to stewardship review.

terms.name: RouteBindingChange
terms.definition: A desired-state declaration binding an ingress route to a tenant. Route bindings resolve tenant context and are therefore as security-relevant as any data-plane write, so they inherit the full declaration machinery — scope, approval rigor, supersession — rather than being distributed configuration with no approver behind it.

constraints.message: A route-binding change must declare exactly one ingress route.

terms.name: Subscription
terms.definition: A first-class, scope-free record of a tenant holding a platform capability, with an access-relevant lifecycle (no billing states) and human-approved activation. Where the tenant can actually use the capability is computed: subscription ∩ entitlement grants ∩ offerings. Subscriptions target capabilities only — applications are owned, not subscribed.

constraints.message: A subscription must have exactly one subscribing tenant.
A subscription must target exactly one capability — bundles expand before subscriptions exist.
A subscription must have exactly one lifecycle state.
Active subscription activation lacks approval by a human principal — a tenant gaining a capability is a meta-authorization boundary.
Active subscription lacks an active subscription for its hard dependency — the closure is auto-included and materialized at subscription time.

terms.name: SubscriptionState
terms.definition: Access-relevant lifecycle state of a subscription; members are individuals (Requested, Active, Suspended, Terminated).

terms.name: TenantMembership
terms.definition: A governed record that a principal may act for a tenant, in a stated capacity, with a lifecycle and a human approval. Entitlement grants are held by tenants; membership is the separate fact that connects the principal a token resolves to with the tenant a route resolves to. Without it an admission decision can verify what a tenant is entitled to, but not that this principal may act for that tenant at all. One principal may hold memberships in several tenants — the consultant and dual-capacity cases are ordinary, not exceptional.

constraints.message: A tenant membership must admit exactly one principal.
A tenant membership must name exactly one tenant.
A tenant membership must have exactly one lifecycle state.
Active tenant membership lacks approval by a human principal — admitting a principal to act for a tenant is a meta-authorization boundary.
Principal holds more than one active membership in the same tenant — which membership authorises a request would be ambiguous.

terms.name: approvedAtTime
terms.definition: Instant at which an approval was given.

terms.name: changeTicket
terms.definition: Reference to the change-management record in the firm's change system, for auditability.

terms.name: inEnvironment
terms.definition: Environment facet of a scope node (e.g., 'prod', 'uat', 'dev'), for cross-cutting queries; the tree carries containment, facets carry dimensions. To be promoted to a SKOS scheme before stable.

terms.name: inRegion
terms.definition: Region facet of a scope node (e.g., 'US', 'EU'), for cross-cutting queries. To be promoted to a SKOS scheme before stable.

terms.name: isolationModel
terms.definition: Tenant-isolation model a capability declares ('shared' or 'cell-per-tenant'); the data-driven fact one SPARQL invariant enforces on the capability's data planes.

terms.name: memberCapacity
terms.definition: Capacity in which the principal acts for the tenant (for example 'employee', 'contractor', 'delegate'). Descriptive at the platform layer: capacity does not grant anything by itself, and what it means inside an application is Level-3.

terms.name: requestCount
terms.definition: Number of requests aggregated in a usage observation window.

terms.name: requiresHumanApproval
terms.definition: Whether declarations bound to this scope (or its descendants, by inheritance up the tree to the nearest ancestor that says anything) require a human approval. Data-driven rigor: prod's subtree says true, dev's says false — one invariant, no shape exceptions.

terms.name: windowEnd
terms.definition: End of a usage observation's aggregation window.

terms.name: windowStart
terms.definition: Start of a usage observation's aggregation window.

terms.name: actuates
terms.definition: Data plane a control plane is the designated writer for. Governance is separated from actuation: only capability control planes actuate (enforced in SHACL).

terms.name: administers
terms.definition: Administrative scope a component or principal is authorized to manage.

terms.name: approvedBy
terms.definition: Principal who gave an approval.

terms.name: bundlesCapability
terms.definition: Capability included in a bundle.

terms.name: changedPolicy
terms.definition: Policy mutated by a change event.

terms.name: declarationScope
terms.definition: Administrative scope a declaration is bound to — mandatory, exactly one (SHACL); 'global' means explicitly naming the root scope, never omitting the triple. Locality: a mutation's data plane must fall inside its declaration's scope.

terms.name: declaredThrough
terms.definition: Management control plane through which a desired-state declaration was authored and governed.

terms.name: declaresDefinition
terms.definition: Authentication journey definition whose intended shape a journey-definition change declares.

terms.name: declaresRouteBinding
terms.definition: Ingress route whose tenant binding a route-binding change declares. Typing enforced in SHACL, not via rdfs:range.

terms.name: declaresStateOf
terms.definition: Data plane whose intended state a declaration describes.

terms.name: dependsOn
terms.definition: Hard dependency between capabilities: the dependent cannot be provisioned without the dependency. Hard-only until a real soft case appears; the dependency graph must be acyclic (SHACL).

terms.name: executedBy
terms.definition: Principal (often a workload/agent) that executed the change.

terms.name: forApplication
terms.definition: Application a declaration provisions for, or that an enablement enables. Makes per-application decommissioning and blast radius a precise query.

terms.name: frontedBy
terms.definition: Authorized party that fronts a portal on one delivery channel. A portal's channels are derived from its fronts' bindings — stated once, never duplicated on the portal.

terms.name: governsCapability
terms.definition: Capability whose configuration and data planes a capability control plane governs.

terms.name: groupsApplication
terms.definition: Application presented within a portal.

terms.name: hasApproval
terms.definition: Approval attached to a change event.

terms.name: hasMembershipState
terms.definition: Current lifecycle state of a tenant membership.

terms.name: hasSubscriptionState
terms.definition: Current lifecycle state of a subscription.

terms.name: justifiedBy
terms.definition: Subscription that justifies a tenant-provisioning declaration. Teardown declarations reference the terminated subscription; provisioning requires an active one.

terms.name: memberOfTenant
terms.definition: Tenant a membership admits the principal to act for.

terms.name: memberPrincipal
terms.definition: Principal a tenant membership admits — the party that may act for the tenant.

terms.name: mutatedDataPlane
terms.definition: Data plane a mutation event wrote into.

terms.name: observedApplication
terms.definition: Application a usage observation concerns.

terms.name: observedCapability
terms.definition: Capability a usage observation saw exercised.

terms.name: ofApplication
terms.definition: Application a capability requirement belongs to.

terms.name: offeredInScope
terms.definition: Scope (and thereby its subtree) in which the offering makes the capability available.

terms.name: offersCapability
terms.definition: Capability an offering makes available.

terms.name: realizesCapability
terms.definition: Capability a data plane is a runtime realization of.

terms.name: realizesIntent
terms.definition: Desired-state declaration a data-plane mutation actuates. Every mutation must carry this trace (no orphan writes).

terms.name: requiredCapability
terms.definition: Capability a requirement names.

terms.name: scopeIncludes
terms.definition: Resource included in an administrative scope.

terms.name: servesTenant
terms.definition: Tenant whose workload or data a data plane serves. Cardinality expresses the capability's isolation model (shared plane vs. per-tenant cell) and is constrained per capability in SHACL, not here.

terms.name: subScopeOf
terms.definition: Parent scope in the single-parent scope tree. The tree carries authority, locality containment, and approval-rigor inheritance; environment/region facets on scope nodes carry cross-cutting dimensions. Single-parent by design — DAG inheritance is ambiguous.

terms.name: subscribedCapability
terms.definition: Capability a subscription holds. Hard dependencies are auto-included as their own subscriptions at subscription time (closure, materialized).

terms.name: subscriber
terms.definition: Tenant holding a subscription — including the platform tenant, which subscribes to its own capabilities so every coverage rule stays uniform.

terms.name: supersedes
terms.definition: Prior declaration this immutable declaration replaces. Realizing a superseded declaration is a warning (reconciler lag); realizing an unapproved one is a violation.
